transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-09-16 14:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Omar Ruiz, Lina Park (Redwood) -- Dr. Priya Malik, Tom Reynolds, Sara Li, Evan Brooks (Vanguard Labs)

Summary: Quick sync on weekly POC QA runs. Found a few regressions on intent classification for 'billing' vs 'clinical' intents after prompt tuning. Discussed guardrail false positives and next steps.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 45 minutes, quick roll call?
[00:07] Dr. Priya Malik: Yep Priya here.
[00:09] Tom Reynolds: Tom, hi.
[00:11] Sara Li: Sara here.
[00:12] Evan Brooks: Evan.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Great. Omar, Lina with me?
[00:16] Omar Ruiz: Yep Omar here, good afternoon.
[00:18] Lina Park: Lina on the call.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Cool, agenda is quality eval recap, regression checks, prompt set changes, and security questions. I'll hand to Omar for the results.
[00:30] Omar Ruiz: Cool, thanks. So we re-ran the 1k test harness with the updated prompts you sent last week - the scoring sheet is attached in the drive link, I think Maya pasted it in the invite - overall precision stayed similar, recall dropped for the billing intent from 0.86 to 0.72, so that's our biggest regression. There's also an uptick in guardrail triggers, mostly around PHI redaction heuristics marking system logs as sensitive.
[01:02] Dr. Priya Malik: Interesting, we were hoping the prompt change would improve disambiguation around clinical vs billing. Any idea why recall fell?
[01:10] Omar Ruiz: A couple things: the new negative examples in the prompt look to have steered the model more conservative, so it's preferring clinical labels less often. Also there's some tokenization weirdness in the prefix - in our infra runs the KV cache prefix sometimes had newline markers that the model treated as signal.
[01:29] Tom Reynolds: When you say KV cache prefix, are you referring to Redwood's prefix caching? We call it the prefix cache in our tests.
[01:34] Omar Ruiz: Yes, Redwood's KV cache - kinda the same thing, sometimes the tokenizer preserves whitespace and that affects scoring.
[01:40] Evan Brooks: Are these tests on hosted or dedicated? Latency differences could be masking behavior.
[01:44] Omar Ruiz: These were on dedicated pool with quantization=4bit and batching set to 8, tail latencies were fine, avg token rate matched expectations - but dedicated environment also had a slightly different kernel selection that might change floating point rounding and therefore boundary classification.
[02:03] Sara Li: From security side, is any PHI leaving their VPC during the run? We need assurance before we run the 5k.
[02:10] Maya Chen: All runs in the POC are in our Dedicated environment with VPC peering; by default no customer data is persisted outside the cluster, and we can enable customer-managed KMS. We'll share SOC2 docs, but Omar will provide the run config.
[02:25] Omar Ruiz: I'll attach the run config and the dedicated pool logs. Note: we did enable prefix caching to test perf; we can re-run with caching off to see if recall improves.
[02:34] Dr. Priya Malik: I'd like that - also can you show examples of false positives on guardrails? We saw a few clinician notes flagged as PHI even when redaction not required.
[02:42] Omar Ruiz: Yeah I'll paste the top 10 FP cases in the doc. Quick note, some of the guardrail false positives came from the heuristic that flags anything with numeric sequences + 'pt' as PHI, which in our dataset catches 'pt' for 'patient' but also 'pt' as 'point' in measurement contexts.
[03:02] Tom Reynolds: We can add a post-check to disambiguate measurement contexts but ideally guardrails are stricter.
[03:07] Lina Park: Quick question on scoring: current rubric uses weighted F1 with class weights tuned by you, Priya requested recall focus for clinical intents - did we change weights?
[03:17] Omar Ruiz: We moved class weight to 0.6 recall, 0.4 precision for clinical but apparently the prompt modifications had bigger effect. So rubric changed but model behavior shifted more.
[03:27] Dr. Priya Malik: We absolutely need recall for clinical, missing a clinical intent is riskier. Can we revert to previous prompt baseline for clinical and A/B test?
[03:36] Maya Chen: Yes we can run an A/B: baseline prompt vs new prompt across same 1k samples and give disaggregated metrics. We'll also surface per-class ROC curves.
[03:45] Evan Brooks: Also curious on regression detection - is Redwood running continuous evals and alerting when metric drops?
[03:51] Omar Ruiz: We have an eval harness that runs nightly and pushes alerts to PagerDuty if drift exceeds thresholds; for POCs we can set lower thresholds and notify you in Slack. There was an anomaly but it didn't breach the current alert threshold.
[04:05] Sara Li: Can you confirm audit logs show inference input hashed and not stored in plaintext? That's critical.
[04:11] Maya Chen: Yes, inputs can be hashed and stored only as token counts, we can provide the audit log format sample.
[04:17] Tom Reynolds: On latency vs cost, earlier tests on quantized models were promising but we saw occasional high tail latency; do you know root cause?
[04:26] Omar Ruiz: Tail latencies usually come from kernel fallbacks when sequence lengths spike; in dedicated pools we can pin kernel variants to avoid fallback but that increases cost. Also batching policies - a misconfigured batch timeout can add 50-200ms.
[04:40] Dr. Priya Malik: Would caching prefix solve any of that?
[04:44] Omar Ruiz: Yes, prefix/KV caching reduces per-token compute for repeated context, so it helps both cost and avg latency but can introduce prefix-effects on scoring as mentioned.
[04:53] Evan Brooks: For the 5k run - can you include runs with caching on and off and both quantized and fp16 baseline? We want to see differences.
[04:59] Omar Ruiz: Yes we'll run four conditions: caching on/off x quant=4bit vs fp16. We'll collect precision/recall per intent and latency/cost per token.
[05:10] Lina Park: Back to guardrails - are you using rule-based redaction then model-based labeling or both?
[05:14] Omar Ruiz: Hybrid: rule-based prefilter then model scoring for ambiguous cases. The FP spike suggests we need to tune the rules to context.
[05:23] Sara Li: From security, what's the plan for key management? We need KMS with customer-controlled keys and HSM option.
[05:29] Maya Chen: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; we'll share the integration guide and ensure the POC uses your key.
[05:35] Dr. Priya Malik: Good. Question on metrics: can you give example failure cases you saw for billing vs clinical?
[05:41] Omar Ruiz: Sure I'll read a couple: sample 172 'patient billed yesterday, please reconcile' was flagged as billing in baseline but new prompt marked as clinical because prompt added more clinical-negative examples that biased toward clinical maybe too strongly in certain phrasing.
[05:58] Tom Reynolds: That feels like prompt leakage where negative examples overwhelm signal.
[06:02] Maya Chen: We can try weight tuning in the prompt instead of adding more examples; soft instructions vs hard examples.
[06:09] Evan Brooks: Also would be useful to get per-token logprobs for ambiguous cases for more granular diagnostics.
[06:14] Omar Ruiz: We'll include logprobs for top-k tokens for the 5k run where possible. Might be large logs but useful.
[06:21] Dr. Priya Malik: What's the timeline for the next deliverable?
[06:24] Maya Chen: We'll send updated prompt CSV and scoring rubric by Monday 9/20, Omar runs the 5k and returns results by 9/24, security docs out by 9/18, and we'll reconvene next week - same time. Does that work?
[06:36] Dr. Priya Malik: Yes that's good.
[06:38] Tom Reynolds: Works for us.
[06:40] Sara Li: Fine.
[06:41] Maya Chen: Quick follow: any blockers on your side for the larger runs?
[06:46] Tom Reynolds: Need final sign-off from infra to allow Redwood dedicated pool to access test VPC; we'll get that today.
[06:52] Evan Brooks: We'll also prepare a list of edge-case prompts we want included; I'll add those to the sheet.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:00] Dr. Priya Malik: One last thing - can we add a guardrail exemption list for known benign patterns to reduce FP rate?
[07:06] Omar Ruiz: Yes we can add whitelist patterns and also a small rule engine to check context. We'll propose a list with the false positive examples.
[07:14] Maya Chen: Ok I'm going to do a quick recap and next steps.
[07:17] --- Recap ---
[07:18] Maya Chen: Actions: 1) Redwood share updated prompt set + rubric (Maya) by 2026-09-20; 2) Redwood run 5k benchmark with caching on/off and quant/fp16 (Omar) by 2026-09-24 and share logs; 3) Redwood share SOC2 + KMS guide (Maya) by 2026-09-18; 4) Vanguard to confirm infra VPC peering (Tom) by 2026-09-17; 5) Vanguard to share regulatory/residency requirements (Sara) by 2026-09-21.
[07:44] Lina Park: Thanks everyone.
[07:46] Dr. Priya Malik: Thanks.
[07:47] Maya Chen: Thanks all, talk next week.
